$comment: The source of @krizaka/fonts, written by hand. scripts/subset.py reads it to cut the files (files/, src/faces.json); scripts/build.mjs merges both into dist/. The words (description, why, use, avoid, rules) are the documentation of ui.krizaka.com/foundations/typography.

families.description: The voice of the headlines: titles, the names of things, figures on a plate. One weight, never bold.
families.why: A heavy old-style serif with round, inked terminals: it reads like a title set in a notebook or a field guide, not like a software template. It has one weight on purpose — hierarchy comes from size and space, never from a bolder cut. It replaces Plus Jakarta Sans, the display face of a thousand templates (#417, ADR-004).
use: Headings and hero lines (display-*, title-*)
Figures on a plate or a tag
The name of a product, a component, a section
avoid: Paragraphs and long reading (use the text face)
Bold or synthetic weights: it has one weight (font-synthesis is off)

families.designer: Braille Institute, Applied Design Works, Elliott Scott, Megan Eiswerth, Linus Boman, Theodore Petrosky
families.description: The reading face: paragraphs, interface, forms, tables.
families.why: Drawn by the Braille Institute so that every letter is told apart from its neighbours (I l 1, O 0, b d p q) by readers with low vision: accessibility as a visible trait, which suits a kit that promises WCAG 2.2 AA. Its quirky, distinct shapes give the text a voice Inter never had.
use: Body text, interface, forms, tables (body-*, caption)
Numbers that must align: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`
Every size from 12 px

families.description: The typewriter of the notebook: specimen tags, captions, footnotes, marginalia, code.
families.why: A Courier redrawn for screens: the typed label of a specimen tag, a caption under a plate, a page number in the margin. It sets code too, in lower case and at reading size. It replaces JetBrains Mono, whose uppercase tracked overlines were one of the template tells (#417).
use: Specimen tags, captions, footnotes, marginalia (note, caption)
Code blocks and inline code (mono-*)
Identifiers, versions, run ids, page numbers

families.description: The product register's headline face (ADR-006): the titles of a signed-in product at 550, 650 and 700. Not for the Cahier sites, which keep Young Serif.
families.why: Oussama tested it on the calm product mockup and wants it: compact, slightly squared bowls and flat terminals, tight and dense without decoration — a working title face for a product where Young Serif's notebook voice would be a costume. It comes back for the products only (ADR-006 §2, amending ADR-004); on the sites it stays « the trio of a thousand templates ». If it still reads as a template, going back is one token: `--kz-font-display: var(--kz-font-sans)`.
use: Product headings and page titles at 550 / 650 / 700, with −0.015 em from 24 px and −0.022 em from 40 px
Big figures: a statistic's value, a price
The name of a thing in a card or a sheet
avoid: The Cahier sites (www, the blog, ui., java., ts., motion): Young Serif is their display
Weight 800, which is the template look; set it at 550 to 700
Paragraphs and long reading (use the text face)

families.description: Legacy (before 0.3.0): The reading face: paragraphs, interface, forms, tables, captions.
families.why: Drawn for screens: a tall x-height, open apertures and tabular figures that line up amounts. It was already the default of @krizaka/tokens and Orazaka's text face, and krizaka.com's body already asked for its character variants (cv02–cv04: open 4, 6 and 9). Cut at the text optical size (opsz 14).
use: Body text, interface, forms, tables (body-*, caption)
Numbers that must align: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`
Every size from 12 px
avoid: Letter-spacing on body sizes beyond the scale's own

families.description: Legacy (before 0.3.0): Code, identifiers, endpoints, and the small uppercase overlines that label a section.
families.why: Used by every Krizaka surface already (krizaka.com, Orazaka). A tall x-height and unambiguous 0/O, 1/l/I make code and identifiers readable at 12 px; its rectangular forms sit well next to the cut corners.
use: Code blocks and inline code (mono-*)
Endpoints, ids, versions, keys
Overlines: uppercase, tracked (overline)

families.designer: Impallari Type, Pablo Impallari, Rodrigo Fuenzalida (Caveat); derived by Krizaka
families.description: The pen of the notebook: margin marks (§ 4), rule numbers, page folios (page 4 sur 6), handwritten notes and stamps, the café chalkboard line. A sparing accent, never reading text.
families.why: A neat handwritten pen, the kind written in a notebook margin: readable at small sizes, full Latin for French accents, lining and tabular figures, and the § sign. Derived from Caveat (SIL OFL 1.1) and renamed Krizaka Cahier as the licence asks: one weight at our ink, line metrics that sit on the 8 px ruled grid, figures of one width so folios and rule numbers align. It is the voice of the Cahier identity (ADR-004) where a person would write by hand, and it also sets the chalkboard line of Yororis.
use: Margin marks (§ 4), rule numbers and page folios (page 4 sur 6)
A handwritten note or a stamp (Fait à Montréal)
The chalkboard line of a café: one short line per screen
Sizes from 20 px
avoid: Headings (use the display face) and paragraphs, interface, forms, tables, buttons (use the text face)
More than one handwritten line per block
Sizes under 18 px, uppercase runs, bold or synthetic weights (it has one weight)

fallbacks.$comment: Measured on the system files (Arial 7.00, Courier New 6.00 of macOS) by scripts/subset.py --measure-fallbacks: units per em and the weighted average advance (FREQUENCIES of subset.py).

rules: Three families, three jobs: display names (Young Serif), text reads (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next), mono types the notes (Courier Prime: tags, captions, footnotes, code). A fourth, the pen (Krizaka Cahier, `--kz-font-cahier`), exists for margin marks, folios, handwritten notes and a chalkboard line and nothing else: never headings, never body text, never interface. A fifth role belongs to the products only (ADR-006): `product-display`, Plus Jakarta Sans, for their titles.
Use the scale, not sizes: `text-display-xl`, `text-body-md`… carry size, line height, weight and tracking together. A one-off size is a missing step — ask for it.

Display has one weight (400) and is never bold, never uppercase: hierarchy comes from size and space. Text from 12 px, at 400–700. The one exception is a product's title face (`product-display`, Plus Jakarta Sans), set at 550, 650 or 700 — never 800 — with −0.015 em from 24 px and −0.022 em from 40 px.
No uppercase tracked overline above every heading: a section is numbered in the margin (§ 2) or not at all. A label is lower case, in the note face.
One display line per block. The rest is text: a page of headlines reads as noise.
Amounts, counters and tables use tabular figures (`tabular-nums`); prices keep the currency from @krizaka/intl, never a hand-written sign.
Measure: 60–75 characters per line for reading (`max-w-prose`); line heights land on the 8 px ruling.

Products wear the product register (ADR-006): `--kz-font-display` is `--kz-font-product-display` (Plus Jakarta Sans), identifiers and tabular meta (« KZ-03 », a reference, a time) are Courier Prime (`--kz-font-mono-meta`), code is the system monospace, eyebrows are the sans, and the pen (Krizaka Cahier) is never inside a product. A product may still override the display role with its own face through `--kz-font-display`; text stays Krizaka's. Never Google Fonts, never a font file committed in an app.
The Krizaka wordmark is drawn, inside the logo: never set the name in a font to imitate it.
